question: Season 1 episodes 4 and 6 are officially "Motendo / Lifedeath – Part 1" and "Lifedeath – Part 2" (en dash), but the app has "Lifedeath, Part 1/2". Do you want the official en-dash form or the app's own ", Part N" style? The app uses that style for multi-part episodes everywhere (Wikipedia gives "Tolerance Is Extinction" as one title split into parts).
options: Keep the app style ", Part N"
Use the official "Motendo / Lifedeath – Part 1" and "Lifedeath – Part 2"
evidence: X-Men '97 season 1 episode table: Title_2 = Lifedeath – Part 1; Title = Lifedeath – Part 2 (the Disney+ episode citation uses the same title).

question: The official multi-part episode titles use an en dash ("Lifedeath – Part 1", "Lifedeath – Part 2", "Tolerance Is Extinction – Part 1/2/3"); the app writes them with a comma ("Lifedeath, Part 2", "Tolerance Is Extinction, Part 1"). Switch to the en-dash form, or keep the comma form as the app's house style?

Wikipedia lists those as separate pilot movies and gives season 1 (1978) as 10 episodes. In the same Incursions box, The Amazing Spider-Man (1977) leaves out its pilot movie. Should the Hulk pilots stay in season 1?
options: Keep [12, 22, 23, 18, 7] with the pilots in season 1 (the DVD set convention)
Change to [10, 22, 23, 18, 7] and leave out the pilots, as with The Amazing Spider-Man (1977)
evidence: Wikipedia's series overview: pilot movies Nov 4 and Nov 28, 1977 (no season), season 1 episodes = 10, season 2 = 22, season 3 = 23, season 4 = 18, season 5 = 7. Every episode name and its order in the app otherwise match exactly.

question: episodes_per_season is [13, 13, 13, 13, 13], one group for each hero (Captain America, Hulk, Iron Man, Thor, Sub-Mariner). The show actually had one season of 65 episodes (Sept 5 to Dec 2, 1966). If the app labels these groups as Seasons 1 to 5, that's wrong. Keep the hero groups or make it one season?
options: Keep the five 13-episode hero groups (fine if they're not labelled as seasons)
Change to one season of 65 episodes in the same order

Replace any that are trailer-only or paraphrased with a line confirmed on screen
evidence: ch-10 'The Avengers are not coming.': not in Wikiquote's Thunderbolts* page (closest: Mel, 'No one else is coming to save the day'). Falcon & Winter Soldier: Sam's 'Co-workers.' is on screen (to Bucky's 'we're partners'), but 'Friends is a stretch' is not found. Moon Knight 'Your mind, I feel it. Fractured. Broken.': not on the Moon Knight, Arthur Harrow or Khonshu quote pages (if it is Harrow's, it is not the box's character either). Eternals 'Throughout the years, we have never interfered... until now.': not found in the film's quotes (looks like teaser narration). FoX-Men 'You're in my school for the gifted...': not on Wikiquote's X-Men (2000) or X-Men: The Animated Series pages. Defenders 'This is what we get, isn't it?...': no Wikiquote page; not found on the MCU wiki.
